title: Normalized strict scalar pullback tower, cone and descent data
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an embedding $\iota:E\to L$, and a scheme map $g:X\to Y$. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $R_W,S_W$ and ordinary and derived scalar extension $S_W(-),C_W(-)$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], the finite pullback towers $D_E,D_L$, their Roos functors $A_E,A_L$, and good (flat-term K-flat) complexes of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The source tower is $D_E(P)$ with termwise $S_X$, and the target tower is $D_L(S_Y(P))$. Define the product comparison by tensoring each projection, and write $b_T=1-s_T$. The generator condition on a tower map $d$ sends $\operatorname{gen}_E(p,a,b)\otimes s$ to $\operatorname{gen}_L(p\otimes1,\iota_n(a),\iota_n(b)\pi^L_n(s))$, where the finite-scalar generator is [def-pod-scalar-pullback-generator]. A cone isomorphism $\kappa:S_X A_E\cong\operatorname{Roos}(S_XD_E)$ has the prescribed coordinates when its first and shifted second coordinates equal the tensor/product comparisons in degrees $i$ and $i-1$. Define $\delta=\kappa;\operatorname{Roos}(d)$. A derived transformation $\tau:C_X Lg_E^*\to Lg_L^* C_Y$ descends $\delta$ when, on every good $P$ whose scalar extension is good, $\tau_{[P]};Lg_L^*(\epsilon_{Y,P});\beta_{L,S_YP}=C_X(\beta_{E,P});\epsilon_{X,A_EP};[\delta_P]$, with $\beta$ the published pullback comparisons and $\epsilon$ the published scalar counits. Strict cone data comprise $d$, its generator equation, $\kappa$, both coordinate equations, $\tau$ and this descent equation. The association condition is the ordinary natural isomorphism $S_{LF}S_{EL}\cong S_{EF}$ sending $(p\otimes s)\otimes z$ to $p\otimes(j(s)z)$. The composition condition asserts existence of these normalized associators on $X,Y$, with the successive level and cone maps equal to the direct maps after these associators. The unit condition asserts the analogous level and cone equations for $L=E$ under the published scalar multiplication unitors. These are definitions only; no witness of strict cone data is chosen.
